title: Blink: External LED
description: Wire an LED and a 220 ohm resistor to pin 13 of an Arduino Uno and run the classic Blink sketch to turn it on and off once a second.

steps.clip: Let's grab everything we need: an Arduino Uno, a breadboard, a 220 ohm resistor, and an LED.
Push one leg of the resistor into the breadboard, then run a wire from that same column to pin 13 on the Arduino.
hints: Either leg of the resistor works first — it has no direction.
Run the wire from the resistor's column straight to digital pin 13.

steps.clip: Bend the resistor's other leg down into a fresh column further along the breadboard.
hints: Give it its own column — don't reuse the column pin 13 is wired to.
No wire needed yet, just seat the leg.

steps.clip: Push the LED's long leg, the anode, into that same column as the resistor's free leg.
hints: The longer leg is the anode — it goes toward the resistor, not GND.
Sharing a column with the resistor's leg wires them together automatically.

steps.clip: Push the LED's short leg into a new column, then wire that column to GND on the Arduino.
hints: The shorter leg is the cathode — it must reach ground or the LED won't light.
Any GND pin on the Uno works.

steps.clip: Now let's upload the code and watch the LED blink on and off once a second.
